standard_prerequisites.name: The spectrum of a ring is a spectral space, and the trace of a henselian pair on an integral extension is again henselian
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, the lemma that the spectrum of a ring is spectral; More on Algebra, the lemma that an integral extension of a henselian pair is henselian, and the lemma that closed subsets meeting the fibre of a henselian pair stay connected
standard_prerequisites.use: Supply the connectedness of the trace of the closure of a point with the closed fibre, which is the hypothesis of the topological statement, and the persistence of the henselian property along finite morphisms.

standard_prerequisites.name: The topological statement for the Zariski site
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the lemma proving the equality of sections over X and over Z for sheaves on the Zariski site under the connectedness hypothesis
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the equality of sections over the small Zariski site of X and of Z.

standard_prerequisites.name: Gabber's comparison statement for the h-topology
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the lemma allowing the passage from the Zariski statement on all finite morphisms to the etale statement
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the final step transferring the verified Zariski statement for all finite morphisms X' -> X to the etale topology.

core_obligations: Collect the topological input (proof lines 15186-15192): the spectrum of any ring is a spectral space, and for a henselian pair (A, I) the intersection of the closure of any point x with the closed fibre Z is connected, by the cited results on henselian pairs.

Verify the statement on the Zariski site (proof lines 15192-15196): the connectedness just recalled is exactly the hypothesis of the cited topological lemma, so Gamma(X, F) = Gamma(Z, F|_Z) holds for sheaves on X_{Zar}.

Extend to all finite morphisms over X (proof lines 15196-15198): for a finite morphism X' -> X one has X' = Spec(A') and Z x_X X' = Spec(A'/IA') with (A', IA') again a henselian pair, so the same Zariski statement holds on (X')_{Zar}.
Pass to the etale topology (proof lines 15198-15199): having the Zariski statement for every finite morphism over X, Gabber's comparison lemma yields the stated equality for sheaves on X_etale.
proof_roadmap: Recall that the trace of the closure of a point on the closed fibre is connected and that henselian pairs persist along integral extensions.
Apply the topological lemma on the Zariski site.
Verify the same statement after every finite base change and invoke the comparison with the etale topology.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for a henselian pair (A, I) with X = Spec(A) and Z = Spec(A/I), the sections of any sheaf F on X_etale over X agree with the sections of its restriction over Z (statement lines 15179-15184). The proof (proof lines 15186-15199) reduces to the Zariski statement using the connectedness of the trace of the closure of a point on the closed fibre, verifies it after every finite base change, and applies Gabber's comparison lemma for the h-topology. H2: a reduction through a topological statement and an induction over finite morphisms, written out in full.
